questions.answer: Two M+ peaks: m/z 78 (35Cl, relative height 3) and m/z 80 (37Cl, relative height 1).
steps: 2-chloropropane C3H7Cl has M = 78 with 35Cl and 80 with 37Cl.
Ratio of 35Cl to 37Cl atoms is 3:1.
So the peak at m/z 78 is three times taller than the peak at m/z 80.
Peaks: m/z 78 (height 3) and m/z 80 (height 1).

questions.question: Show the initiation step for propane reacting with chlorine, including arrows and conditions.
questions.answer: Cl2 -> 2Cl. (under UV light), using fish-hook arrows for homolytic fission.
steps: Conditions: ultraviolet (UV) light.
Cl-Cl bond breaks homolytically.
Each Cl atom takes one electron from the bond (fish-hook arrows).
Initiation: Cl2 -> 2Cl. (radicals).

questions.question: Using the initiation step, state what is meant by homolytic and by free radical.
questions.answer: Homolytic: a covalent bond breaks with each atom taking one electron. Free radical: a species with an unpaired electron.
steps: In homolytic fission the shared pair splits evenly.
Each atom receives one electron.
A free radical is a species with one or more unpaired electrons.
Cl. is a free radical.

questions.question: Suggest why free radical chlorination has limited use in organic synthesis.
questions.answer: It gives a mixture of products (multiple substitution and isomers), so the yield of the desired product is low.
steps: Radicals react with the alkane at many positions.
Further substitution gives multiple chlorinated products.
So a mixture forms that is hard to separate.
The yield of the desired product is low.

questions.question: Give the mechanism for propene reacting with HCl to form 2-chloropropane, with curly arrows, dipoles and lone pairs.
questions.answer: Electrophilic addition: H+ adds to C1, forming the secondary carbocation CH3CH+CH3, which Cl- attacks to give 2-chloropropane.
steps: HCl is polar: Hdelta+ - Cldelta-.
The C=C pi electrons attack Hdelta+ (arrow from C=C to H).
H bonds to C1, leaving the secondary carbocation CH3CH+CH3 (arrow from H-Cl to Cl-).
Cl- lone pair attacks C+ (arrow), giving 2-chloropropane.

questions.question: Explain why only a small amount of 1-chloropropane is produced.
questions.answer: The secondary carbocation formed is more stable than the primary one needed for 1-chloropropane, so 2-chloropropane forms preferentially.
steps: 1-chloropropane requires a primary carbocation intermediate.
2-chloropropane forms via a secondary carbocation.
Secondary carbocations are more stable (alkyl groups donate electrons).
So the secondary route dominates and 1-chloropropane is minor.

questions.question: State the meaning of the term unsaturated for a fat.
questions.answer: Contains one or more C=C double bonds in the carbon chains.
steps: Unsaturated means not holding the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.
Unsaturated fats contain C=C double bonds.
Each C=C can react with bromine.
So unsaturated = contains at least one C=C.

questions.question: Name the type of reaction used to determine the degree of unsaturation with bromine water.
steps: Bromine adds across each C=C of the fat.
Br2 is an electrophile attacking the pi electrons.
The reaction adds Br atoms without losing any atoms.
So electrophilic addition.

questions.question: Plot a graph of the bromination data (0.5 g fat) and include a line of best fit.
questions.answer: Graph of volume of bromine water / cm3 (y) against average number of C=C bonds per molecule (x), points (1, 28.3), (2, 57.3), (3, 86.9), (4, 115), with a straight line of best fit through the origin (gradient about 29 cm3 per C=C)

Plot the four points accurately
Draw one straight line of best fit; the points are very close to a straight line that passes through (0, 0), since volume is proportional to the number of C=C bonds

questions.question: Calculate the mean volume of bromine water using all results in the margarine bromination table.
steps: Add all four volumes: 36.9 + 34.1 + 39.3 + 32.5 = 142.8 cm3
Divide by 4: 142.8 / 4 = 35.7 cm3

steps: Use the mean volume from part (iii), 35.7 cm3
On the graph read across from 35.7 cm3 on the y axis to the line, then down to the x axis

questions.question: Using the simplest alkene, draw the mechanism for the reaction with liquid bromine.
questions.answer: Ethene + Br2 gives 1,2-dibromoethane via pi attack on the polarised Br2 and Br- attack on the carbocation.
steps: Br2 is polarised by the approaching C=C (induced dipole).
C=C pi electrons attack Brdelta+ (arrow from C=C to Br).
Br-Br breaks heterolytically; Br- takes the electron pair (arrow to Br-).
Br- attacks the carbocation (arrow from lone pair to C+), giving BrCH2CH2Br.

questions.question: Name the product of the reaction in (c)(i) by applying IUPAC rules.
steps: The product is BrCH2CH2Br.
Parent chain ethane (2 C).
Bromines on C1 and C2.
Name: 1,2-dibromoethane.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of trans in trans fats, using a skeletal formula showing four carbon atoms.
questions.answer: In a trans fat the two carbon chains on the C=C lie on opposite sides of the double bond (E configuration).
steps: Draw C1-C2=C3-C4 in a zigzag skeletal formula.
Trans means the main chains (C1 on C2 and C4 on C3) are on opposite sides.
The C=C cannot rotate, so this arrangement is fixed.
Cis fats have both chains on the same side.

questions.question: Draw the displayed formula of the monomers chloroethene (for PVC) and tetrafluoroethene (for PTFE).
steps: PVC is made from chloroethene, CH2=CHCl.
PTFE is made from tetrafluoroethene, CF2=CF2.
Each has one C=C that opens to form the polymer.
Displayed: H2C=CHCl and F2C=CF2 with the double bonds shown.

questions.question: Give one advantage and one disadvantage each for incineration and recycling of polymer waste.
questions.answer: Incineration: advantage energy recovery; disadvantage toxic gases. Recycling: advantage conserves resources; disadvantage sorting and cost, with quality loss.
steps: Incineration recovers heat energy and reduces waste volume.
Incineration releases toxic gases such as HCl and CO2.
Recycling conserves crude oil and reduces landfill.
Recycling needs sorting and can lower polymer quality; any one disadvantage each is acceptable.

questions.question: Deduce possible structures and names for compounds A, B, C and D, all C4H8, where A and B are geometric isomers, C has one C=C but no geometric isomer, and D has no C=C.
questions.answer: A: (Z)-but-2-ene; B: (E)-but-2-ene; C: but-1-ene (or 2-methylpropene); D: cyclobutane (or methylcyclopropane).
steps: A and B are a cis/trans pair, so they are (Z)-but-2-ene and (E)-but-2-ene.
C has one C=C and no geometric isomer, e.g. but-1-ene (or 2-methylpropene).
D has no C=C and C4H8 is one degree of unsaturation: cyclobutane.
Check: each formula is C4H8.

questions.question: Describe the difference between the sigma and pi bonds in a C=C, including a labelled diagram.
questions.answer: Sigma: head-on overlap along the axis, allows free rotation. Pi: sideways overlap of p orbitals above and below the plane, restricts rotation and is weaker.
steps: Sigma bond: head-on overlap of orbitals along the internuclear axis.
Electron density is between the nuclei, and rotation about it is free.
Pi bond: sideways overlap of parallel p orbitals above and below the plane.
Pi bonds are weaker and restrict rotation about the C=C (label both on a diagram).

questions.question: Give two reasons why compounds A and B exist as geometric isomers.
questions.answer: The C=C restricts rotation (pi bond), and each carbon of the C=C has two different groups.
steps: The pi bond prevents rotation about the C=C.
Each C of the C=C carries two different groups (H and CH3).
So the groups are fixed cis or trans.
Both reasons are needed for E/Z isomerism.

questions.question: Name the mechanism and type of reaction for Reaction 1 of propene.
questions.answer: Electrophilic addition (ionic mechanism via a carbocation).
steps: Propene C=C is attacked by an electrophile (H+ from HCl).
The reaction adds across the double bond.
It proceeds through a carbocation intermediate.
So electrophilic addition.

questions.question: Explain why 2-chloropropane forms in greater yield than 1-chloropropane, referring to the intermediates.
questions.answer: The secondary carbocation intermediate is more stable than the primary one, so it forms more readily and gives 2-chloropropane as the major product.
steps: Reaction 1 proceeds via a carbocation intermediate.
Adding H to C1 gives the secondary carbocation CH3CH+CH3.
Adding H to C2 gives the less stable primary carbocation CH3CH2CH2+.
Alkyl groups stabilise the secondary ion more (inductive effect), so 2-chloropropane dominates.

questions.question: Complete the mechanism for the first stage of Reaction 2 (same mechanism as Reaction 1), with intermediate, curly arrows, dipoles, charges and lone pairs.
questions.answer: Step 1: curly arrow from the C=C to the H of H-O (delta+), arrow from the O-H bond to O; intermediate CH3-CH+-CH3 and HOSO2O-; Step 2: lone pair on O- attacks C+, giving CH3CH(OSO2OH)CH3
steps: Mark the polar O-H bond of H2SO4 as H(delta+)-O(delta-); a curly arrow starts at the C=C and ends at the H
A second curly arrow starts at the O-H bond and ends at the O, forming the hydrogensulfate ion HOSO2O- with a lone pair and a negative charge
The H adds to the terminal CH2, leaving the secondary carbocation CH3-CH+-CH3 as the intermediate
Step 2: a curly arrow from a lone pair on the negative O of HOSO2O- to the C+ forms the C-O bond, giving CH3CH(OSO2OH)CH3

questions.question: Name the mechanism and type of reaction when chlorine reacts with butane to form 1-chlorobutane.
steps: Chlorine reacts with a saturated alkane.
Radicals are involved (initiation, propagation, termination).
One H atom is replaced by Cl.
So free radical substitution.

questions.question: Give the essential condition for Step 1 (initiation) to occur.
steps: Step 1 breaks Cl-Cl homolytically.
This needs energy input.
UV light provides the energy.
So UV light.

questions.question: Name the type of step illustrated by Step 3.
steps: Step 3 combines two radicals.
This removes radicals from the chain.
Combining radicals ends the chain reaction.
So termination.

questions.question: Describe the propagation step (the other step type not shown), including two possible examples in this reaction.
questions.answer: Propagation: a radical reacts with a molecule to form a new radical and product, e.g. Cl. + C4H10 -> HCl + C4H9. and C4H9. + Cl2 -> C4H9Cl + Cl.
steps: Propagation steps regenerate a radical, so the chain continues.
Example 1: Cl. + C4H10 -> HCl + C4H9. (H atom abstraction).
Example 2: C4H9. + Cl2 -> C4H9Cl + Cl. (Cl transferred).
Each propagation step uses one radical and produces one radical.

questions.question: State what is meant by a polar molecule, and why chlorine is not polar.
questions.answer: A polar molecule has a permanent dipole (uneven charge distribution). Chlorine is not polar because both atoms have the same electronegativity, so the bond is not polarised.
steps: A polar molecule has a permanent dipole from uneven electron distribution.
This arises from a difference in electronegativity between atoms.
Cl2 has two identical Cl atoms with equal electronegativity.
So the electrons are shared equally and Cl2 is non-polar.

questions.question: Explain why chlorine reacts with alkenes even though it is not polar.
questions.answer: The electron-rich C=C pi bond induces a dipole in the Cl-Cl bond, making one Cl delta+ (an electrophile) that is attacked by the alkene.
steps: The C=C pi electrons are electron-rich.
They polarise the Cl-Cl bond (induced dipole).
One Cl becomes delta+ and acts as an electrophile.
The alkene then adds Cl across the C=C by electrophilic addition.

questions.question: A sample of volatile liquid X: at 473 K and 110 000 Pa, 3.50 g of X occupies 1.79 dm3. Calculate the moles of X (R = 8.31).
Deduce the relative molecular mass of X.
steps: Mr = mass / moles = 3.50 / 0.0501.

questions.question: Compound X contains 85.7 % C and 14.3 % H by mass. Calculate its empirical formula.
steps: Ratio 1 : 2.
Empirical formula CH2.

questions.question: Deduce the molecular formula of X from its empirical formula and Mr.
steps: Empirical formula mass CH2 = 14.0.
Molecular formula C5H10.

questions.question: A purple KMnO4 solution remains purple when shaken with liquid X. State what this shows about X's structure.
questions.answer: X has no C=C double bond, so it is saturated (e.g. a cycloalkane).
steps: Alkenes decolourise acidified KMnO4 (purple to colourless).
The solution stays purple, so no C=C is present.
X with formula C5H10 and no C=C must be a cycloalkane.
So X is saturated (cycloalkane).

questions.question: Identify two possible structural isomers of X (C5H10) consistent with (a)(iv) and (b).
questions.answer: Methylcyclobutane and ethylcyclopropane (any two C5H10 cycloalkanes).
steps: X is C5H10 and does not decolourise KMnO4, so it is a cycloalkane.
Cyclopentane is one option.
Methylcyclobutane and ethylcyclopropane are other C5H10 cycloalkanes.
Name any two.

questions.question: Draw the displayed formulae of chloroethene and one geometric isomer of 1-chloropropene.
questions.answer: Chloroethene: H2C=CHCl. (E)-1-chloropropene: CH3CH=CHCl with CH3 and Cl on opposite sides.
steps: Chloroethene: CH2=CHCl.
1-chloropropene: CH3-CH=CH-Cl.
E isomer: CH3 and Cl on opposite sides of the C=C.
Display with all bonds and the C=C shown.

questions.question: Explain why chloroethene and 1-chloropropene are members of a homologous series.
questions.answer: They have the same functional group (C=C and Cl) and differ by a CH2 unit, so they share a general formula and similar chemistry.
steps: Homologous series: same general formula and functional group.
Chloroethene is C2H3Cl; 1-chloropropene is C3H5Cl.
They differ by one CH2 unit.
Both contain a C=C bonded to Cl, so they have similar chemical properties.

questions.question: Explain why 1-chloropropene exists as two geometric isomers but chloroethene does not.
questions.answer: In chloroethene one carbon of the C=C has two identical H atoms, so no E/Z isomers; in 1-chloropropene each carbon has two different groups (Cl and H; CH3 and H).
steps: E/Z isomerism needs two different groups on each C of the C=C.
Chloroethene: CH2=CHCl; the CH2 carbon has two H atoms, so no isomers.
1-chloropropene: C1 has Cl and H; C2 has CH3 and H.
Both carbons have two different groups, so E and Z isomers exist.

questions.question: Draw the structure of poly(1-chloropropene).
steps: Monomer CH3-CH=CH-Cl has one C=C.
The C=C opens; repeat unit -CH(CH3)-CH(Cl)-.
Join units head to tail.
Result: -[CH(CH3)-CH(Cl)]n-.

questions.question: Suggest two advantages of PVC over metal for water pipes and gutters, other than cost.
questions.answer: PVC does not corrode or rust, and it is lighter and easier to install (it is also a non-conductor).
steps: Metals corrode (rust) in water; PVC does not.
PVC is lighter than metal, so easier to handle and install.
PVC is a good electrical insulator.
Any two of these advantages.
